Standard Library

cache — Thread-safe TTL + LRU in-memory cache

Module cache (lib/cache.lora) exports 25 declarations. Import with use cache;.

Overview

cache provides a thread-safe, TTL-aware, size-bounded LRU in-memory cache (cache::cache) that owns its ^str keys and ^[]u8 byte values.

All operations lock an internal thread::mutex. Every time-sensitive method has both a wall-clock variant (set, get, contains, purge_expired, ttl_remaining) and a deterministic *_at variant taking an explicit now_ns: i64 timestamp for testing or custom clocks. Hit, miss, eviction, and expiration counters are exposed via get_stats.

SymbolPurpose
newCreate a cache (max_cap = 0 unbounded, default_ttl <= 0 no expiry)
set / set_str / set_at / set_str_atInsert or update key/value with optional per-entry TTL
get / get_str / get_at / get_str_atLookup (returns owned ^[]u8 or ^str), promotes LRU, updates stats
peek / peek_at / contains / ttl_remainingInspect without changing recency or hit/miss counters
remove / purge_expired / clearDelete keys or sweep expired entries
get_stats / reset_stats / sizeRead or reset cache::stats

Valid Usage & Examples

Deterministic TTL expiration and purging

Use set_str_at, contains_at, and purge_expired_at with explicit nanosecond timestamps.

lora Allowed 
use cache;
use time;

export fn main() void = {
	let c = cache::new(0z, 10 * time::SECOND);
	let t0 = 1000000000000i64;

	cache::set_str_at(&c, "session", "alice", t0)!;
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "short", "tmp", t0, 2 * time::SECOND)!;
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "perm", "ok", t0, @time::duration(0i64))!;

	assert(!cache::contains_at(&c, "short", t0 + 2 * @i64(time::SECOND)));
	assert(cache::purge_expired_at(&c, t0 + 10 * @i64(time::SECOND)) == 1z);
	assert(cache::size(&c) == 1z);
	assert((cache::get_str_at(&c, "perm", t0 + 999999999i64)! as ^str) == "ok");
}

LRU eviction and hit/miss statistics

Bound the cache by max_cap and inspect cache::stats after hits, misses, and evictions.

lora Allowed 
use cache;

export fn main() void = {
	let c = cache::new(2z);
	let t0 = 100i64;
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "k1", "v1", t0)!;
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "k2", "v2", t0)!;
	let _ = cache::get_str_at(&c, "k1", t0)! as ^str; // hit, k2 becomes LRU
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "k3", "v3", t0)!;            // evicts k2
	let miss = cache::get_str_at(&c, "missing", t0)!;
	assert(miss is void);

	let st = cache::get_stats(&c);
	assert(st.hits == 1u64 && st.misses == 1u64 && st.evictions == 1u64);
}

Disallowed Forms & Diagnostics

Expecting ttl = 0 to expire immediately

In cache, ttl == 0 disables expiration for that entry, and ttl < 0 falls back to default_ttl.

Logic Error: ttl == 0 means no expiration; use a positive duration (e.g., 1ns) to expire after 1ns
lora Rejected 
use cache;
use time;

export fn main() void = {
	let c = cache::new(10z, 5 * time::SECOND);
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "k", "v", 100i64, @time::duration(0i64))!;
	// Wrong assumption: 0ns TTL does NOT expire at t = 200
	assert(!cache::contains_at(&c, "k", 200i64)); // error: ttl == 0 disables expiration, so key is still present
}
lora Allowed 
use cache;
use time;

export fn main() void = {
	let c = cache::new(10z, 5 * time::SECOND);
	cache::set_str_at(&c, "k", "v", 100i64, @time::duration(1i64))!; // ok: positive 1ns TTL expires at t = 101
	assert(!cache::contains_at(&c, "k", 200i64));
}

Constraints & Limits

Thread safety
Mutex-guarded
Every operation locks `c.mu` (`thread::mutex`).
Hash table
Open-addressing
Starts at 16 slots; rehashes when `(count + tombstones + 1) * 10 >= cap * 7`.
TTL overflow
Saturates at MAX_I64
Large `now_ns + ttl` saturates instead of wrapping negative.
Return ownership
Owned ^[]u8 / ^str
`get*` and `peek*` allocate fresh copies for thread safety.
